If time is transmitted in the position report, it is to be made in regard to the reported position (e.g., 'STOCKERAU, THREE MINUTES AGO' or 'STOCKERAU, IN ONE MINUTE'). If the aircraft is beyond three minutes from the reported position, ano
The initial call on WIEN INFORMATION for a flight without a submitted flight plan shall use the phraseology: 'WIEN INFORMATION OEABC NEGATIVE FLIGHT PLAN'.
An example transmission on another ATS frequency is: 'OE-AAA, KREMS, 2000 FT, INFORMATION B FOR LANDING'.
An air traffic control clearance shall indicate aircraft identification as shown in the flight plan.
An air traffic control clearance shall indicate the clearance limit.
An air traffic control clearance shall indicate the route of flight.
The route of flight shall be detailed in each clearance when deemed necessary.
The phrase 'cleared via flight planned route' shall not be used when granting a re-clearance.
An air traffic control clearance shall indicate level(s) of flight for the entire route or part thereof and changes of levels if required.
An air traffic control clearance shall indicate any necessary instructions or information on other matters.
An air traffic control clearance shall include ATFM departure slot if applicable.
An air traffic control clearance shall include the time of expiry of the clearance.
When issuing a clearance covering a requested change in route or level, the exact nature of the change shall be included in the clearance.
When traffic conditions will not permit clearance of a requested change, the word 'UNABLE' shall be used.
When warranted by circumstances, an alternative route or level shall be offered.
Relaying clearances, instructions, or information shall use the phraseology: '(ATC unit) CLEARS/INSTRUCTS/INFORMS (details of the clearance, instructions, or information)'
Confirmation of a readback shall use the phraseology: '[THAT IS] CORRECT'
Rejection of a readback shall use the phraseology: 'NEGATIVE [I SAY AGAIN (ATC unit) CLEARS/INSTRUCTS (details of the clearance or the instruction)]'
If clearance cannot be issued immediately, use the phraseology: 'EXPECT CLEARANCE (or type of clearance) AT (time)/IN (number) MINUTES'
If unable to issue clearance, use the phraseology: 'IF UNABLE/IF NOT POSSIBLE [(alternative instructions) AND] ADVISE'
If unable to issue arrival clearance, use the phraseology: 'UNABLE TO ISSUE (designator) ARRIVAL (reasons)'
If level/route not available, use the phraseology: 'LEVEL/ROUTE NOT AVAILABLE DUE (reason) ALTERNATIVE[S] IS/ARE (routes) ADVISE INTENTIONS'
Note: How to issue a departure clearance is covered in chapters 5.3.1.7.1 (for VFR flights) and 5.7.1.1 (for IFR flights).
The phrase 'REQUEST TO FILE A FLIGHT PLAN' shall be used to request submission of a flight plan.
The phrase 'CHANGE OF FLIGHT PLAN (details)' shall be used to request a change to an existing flight plan.
The phrase 'FLIGHT PLAN RECEIVED' shall be used by ground to acknowledge receipt of a flight plan.
The phrase 'CLOSING MY FLIGHT PLAN' shall be used to close a flight plan during flight without submitting an arrival message or time.
The phrase 'SHORTLY BEFORE LANDING AT (name of aerodrome), REQUEST TO CLOSE MY FLIGHT PLAN' shall be used to close a flight plan shortly before landing.
The phrase 'FLIGHT PLAN CLOSED AT (time)' shall be used by ground to acknowledge closure of a flight plan.
Closing a flight plan terminates alerting service for overdue arrival messages, but search and rescue service remains active.
The phrase '(type of A/C, position, flight rules) (numbers) FEET, WILL ENTER RMZ [FOR LANDING] [AT (aerodrome)] [IN (Name Flugplatz)]' shall be used when entering an RMZ.
The phrase '(type of A/C, position, flight rules) (numbers) FEET, WILL CROSS RMZ (route)' shall be used when crossing an RMZ.
The phrase 'LEAVING RMZ (position) (numbers) FEET' shall be used when leaving an RMZ.
RMZ position reports must be transmitted even if the aeronautical station does not answer.
When cancelling an IFR flight, the pilot shall use the phraseology 'CANCELLING MY IFR FLIGHT' and the controller shall respond with 'IFR FLIGHT CANCELLED AT (time)'.
Cancelling an IFR flight cancels only the IFR portion; the flight plan remains active and an arrival message is required.

If a pilot changing from IFR to VFR is likely unable to maintain VMC, the controller shall provide information using the phraseology: 'INSTRUMENT METEOROLOGICAL CONDITIONS REPORTED/FORECAST IN THE VICINTIY OF (location)'.

When requesting a change from VFR to IFR, the pilot shall use 'REQUEST IFR CLEARANCE' and the controller shall provide a clearance including limit, route, level, squawk code, and IFR start time/position.
When clearing an aircraft for Special VFR, the controller shall use the phraseology 'CLEARED SPECIAL VFR'.
To request confirmation of 8.33 kHz capability, the controller shall use the phraseology 'CONFIRM EIGHT POINT THREE THREE'.
To request confirmation of UHF capability, the controller shall use the phraseology 'CONFIRM UHF'.
To indicate UHF capability, the pilot shall use the phraseology 'AFFIRM UHF'.
To indicate lack of UHF capability, the pilot shall use the phraseology 'NEGATIVE UHF'.
When issuing a clearance to a non-equipped/non-exempted aircraft to prevent entry into mandatory airspace, the controller shall use the phraseology 'DUE EIGHT POINT THREE THREE REQUIREMENT'.
The term 'point' in this context refers only to the 8.33 kHz channel spacing concept and does not change existing ICAO provisions regarding the term 'decimal'.
Aircraft shall use the phraseology 'REQUEST CLIMB/DESCENT [AT (time) /IMMEDIATELY]' to request a level change.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'CLIMB/DESCEND' to issue a climb or descent instruction.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by '[TO] (level)' to specify the target altitude.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'TO AND MAINTAIN BLOCK (level) TO (level)' to specify a block altitude.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'TO REACH (level) AT/BY (time or significant point)' to specify timing.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'REPORT LEAVING/PASSING/REACHING (level)' to require altitude reports.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'AT (number) FEET PER MINUTE [OR GREATER/LESS] METRES PER SECOND' to specify rate.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'STOP CLIMB/DESCENT AT (level)' to terminate the maneuver.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'CONTINUE CLIMB/DESCENT [TO] (level)' to extend the maneuver.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'EXPEDITE CLIMB/DESCENT [UNTIL PASSING (level)]' to request expedited rate.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'REPORT MINIMUM/MAXIMUM RATE OF CLIMB/DESCENT' to request rate reports.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'CLIMB/DESCEND WITH MINIMUM/MAXIMUM RATE OF CLIMB/DESCENT' to specify rate constraints.
Climb/descent instructions may be followed by 'RESUME NORMAL RATE OF DESCENT/CLIMB' to return to standard rates.
ATC shall use 'EXPECT CLIMB/DESCENT AT (time or significant point)' to provide advance notice of a level change.
ATC shall use 'REPORT LEAVING/REACHING/PASSING (level)' to require altitude reports.
ATC shall use 'WHEN READY CLIMB/DESCEND [TO] (level)' to issue a climb/descent instruction contingent on pilot readiness.
ATC shall use 'AFTER PASSING (significant point) CLIMB/DESCEND [TO] (level)' to issue a climb/descent instruction contingent on passing a point.
ATC shall use 'AT (time or significant point) CLIMB/DESCEND [TO] (level)' to issue a climb/descent instruction at a specific time or point.
ATC shall use 'MAINTAIN AT LEAST (number) METRES/FEET ABOVE/BELOW (aircraft call sign)' to require vertical separation from another aircraft.
Aircraft shall use 'REQUEST LEVEL/FLIGHT LEVEL/ALTITUDE CHANGE FROM (name of unit) [AT (time or significant point)]' to request a level change.
ATC shall use 'EXPECT LEVEL CHANGE/CLIMB/DESCENT AT (time or significant point)' to provide advance notice of a level change.
To require an aircraft to climb or descend maintaining own separation and VMC, ATC shall use 'MAINTAIN OWN SEPARATION AND VMC' followed by '[FROM (level)] [TO (level)]' or 'ABOVE/BELOW/TO (level)'.
When in doubt about compliance, ATC shall use 'ADVISE IF ABLE TO CROSS (significant point) AT (time or level)' to query pilot capability.
When in doubt about compliance, ATC shall use 'IF UNABLE (alternative instructions) AND ADVISE' to provide alternatives if the pilot is unable.
When unable to comply with a clearance or instruction, aircraft shall use 'UNABLE'.
When unable to comply with a clearance or instruction, aircraft shall use 'UNABLE (designator) DEPARTURE/ARRIVAL (reasons)' to specify the nature of the inability.
When unable to comply with a clearance or instruction, aircraft shall use 'UNABLE CROSS (significant point) AT/ABOVE/BELOW (level)' to specify inability to cross a point.
To require action at a specific time or place, ATC shall use 'IMMEDIATELY'.
To require action at a specific time or place, ATC shall use 'AFTER PASSING (significant point)'.
To require action at a specific time or place, ATC shall use 'AT (time or significant point)'.
To require action when convenient, ATC shall use 'WHEN READY' (or 'WENN BEREIT' in German context) followed by the instruction.
Phraseology for omitting position reports shall use 'OMIT POSITION REPORTS [UNTIL (specify)]'.
Phraseology for specifying the next report location shall use 'NEXT REPORT [AT] (significant point)'.
Phraseology for restricting reports to specific points shall use 'REPORTS REQUIRED ONLY AT (significant point(s))'.
Phraseology for resuming position reporting shall use 'RESUME POSITION REPORTING'.
The word 'level' in parentheses indicates that specific level information (FLIGHT LEVEL (number) or (number) FEET) must be inserted to complete the phrase.
Phraseology for altitude instructions shall use '[ALTITUDE] (number) FEET/METRES'.
Phraseology for height instructions shall use '[HEIGHT] (number) FEET/METRES'.
Phraseology for reporting flight level/altitude shall use 'REPORT FLIGHT LEVEL/ALTITUDE'.
Phraseology for verifying flight level/altitude shall use 'VERIFY FLIGHT LEVEL/ALTITUDE'.
Phraseology for requesting flight level shall use 'REQUEST FLIGHT LEVEL (level)/(number) FEET'.
Phraseology for passing level information as vertical distance from other traffic shall use '(number) FEET/METRES ABOVE/BELOW'.
Phraseology for maintaining a level shall use 'MAINTAIN (level) [TO (significant point)]'.
Phraseology for maintaining a level until passing a significant point shall use 'MAINTAIN (level) UNTIL PASSING (significant point)'.
Phraseology for maintaining a level for a duration after passing a significant point shall use 'MAINTAIN (level) UNTIL (minutes) AFTER PASSING (significant point)'.
Phraseology for maintaining a level until a specific time shall use 'MAINTAIN (level) UNTIL (time)'.
Phraseology for maintaining a level until further advised shall use 'MAINTAIN (level) UNTIL FURTHER ADVISED'.
Phraseology for maintaining a level while in controlled airspace shall use 'MAINTAIN (level) WHILE IN CONTROLLED AIRSPACE'.
Phraseology for maintaining a block of levels shall use 'MAINTAIN BLOCK (level) TO (level)'.
Phraseology for maintaining a level until advised by a specific unit shall use 'MAINTAIN (level) UNTIL ADVISED BY (name of unit)'.
The term 'MAINTAIN' is not to be used in lieu of 'DESCEND' or 'CLIMB' when instructing an aircraft to change level.
Phraseology for crossing a significant point at/above/below a level shall use 'CROSS (significant point) AT/ABOVE/BELOW (level)'.
Phraseology for crossing a significant point at a time shall use 'CROSS (significant point) AT (time) OR LATER/BEFORE AT (level)'.
Phraseology for crossing a distance shall use 'CROSS (distance) MILES [GNSS/DME] [(direction)] OF (name of DME station) OR (distance) [(direction)] OF (significant point) AT/ABOVE/BELOW (level)'.
Phraseology for cruise climb shall use 'CRUISE CLIMB BETWEEN (levels) (or ABOVE (level))'.

A controlled flight shall report to the appropriate air traffic services unit, as soon as possible, the time and level of passing each designated compulsory reporting point, together with any other required information.
Position reports shall be made in relation to additional points when requested by the appropriate air traffic services unit.
In the absence of designated reporting points, position reports shall be made at intervals prescribed by the competent authority or specified by the appropriate air traffic services unit.
Position reports for IFR flights shall contain aircraft identification.
Position reports for IFR flights shall contain position.
Position reports for IFR flights shall contain actual level or altitude.
Pilots shall provide level information at the nearest full 30 m or 100 ft as indicated on the pilot's altimeter.
Position reports for VFR flights shall contain aircraft identification.
Position reports for VFR flights shall contain position (and time to/from position if aircraft is not exact overhead reported position).
If time is transmitted in the position report it is to be made in regard to the reported position.

To request a report of present position, use phraseology: 'REPORT (GNSS or DME) DISTANCE FROM (significant point or name of DME station)' and reply '(distance) MILES (GNSS or DME) FROM (name of DME station) (or significant point)'.

To request a report at a specified place, use phraseology: 'REPORT ABEAM/PASSING (significant point)' and reply '[ABEAM] (significant point) (level) [SQUAWK (code)]' or 'WILL REPORT ABEAM/PASSING (significant point)'.
To request a report at a specified distance, use phraseology: 'REPORT PASSING (three digits) RADIAL (name of VOR) VOR'.

To request a report of aerodrome in sight, use phraseology: 'REPORT AERODROME (designator) DESTINATION [AERODROME] IN SIGHT' and reply 'WILL REPORT AERODROME (designator)/ DESTINATION [AERODROME] IN SIGHT'.

To omit position reports until a specified position, use phraseology: 'UNTERLASSEN SIE POSITIONSMELDUNGEN [BIS (Details)]' or 'NÄCHSTE MELDUNG [BEI] (markanter Punkt)' or 'POSITIONSMELDUNGEN NUR ÜBER (markante/r Punkt/e) ERFORDERLICH' or 'N
ATC shall use the phraseology 'REPORT SPEED' to instruct a pilot to report speed.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'REPORT INDICATED AIRSPEED/TRUE AIRSPEED/MACH NUMBER' to instruct a pilot to report specific speed types.
Aircraft shall respond to speed requests with 'SPEED (number)/KNOTS/MACH (number) KILOMETRES PER HOUR'.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'MAINTAIN (number) KNOTS/MACH (number)/KILOMETRES PER HOUR [OR GREATER/LESS] [UNTIL (significant point)]' to assign a speed.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'FLY (number) KNOTS/MACH' to assign a speed.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'DO NOT EXCEED (number) KNOTS/MACH (number)/KILOMETRES PER HOUR' to impose a maximum speed.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'MAINTAIN PRESENT SPEED' to instruct an aircraft to keep its current speed.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'INCREASE/REDUCE SPEED TO (number) KNOTS/MACH (number)/KILOMETRES PER HOUR [OR GREATER/LESS]' to adjust speed to a target.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'INCREASE/REDUCE SPEED BY (number) KNOTS/MACH (number)/KILOMETRES PER HOUR' to adjust speed by a delta.
Aircraft shall respond to speed instructions with 'UNABLE, INDICATED AIRSPEED WILL BE (number) KNOTS/MACH (number) KILOMETRES PER HOUR' if unable to comply.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'RESUME NORMAL SPEED' to instruct an aircraft to return to normal speed.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'RESUME PUBLISHED SPEED' to instruct an aircraft to return to published speed.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'REDUCE TO MINIMUM APPROACH SPEED' to instruct an aircraft to reduce to minimum approach speed.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'REDUCE TO MINIMUM CLEAN SPEED' to instruct an aircraft to reduce to minimum clean speed.
Aircraft shall respond to minimum speed instructions with 'MINIMUM CLEAN SPEED/MINIMUM APPROACH SPEED IS (number) KNOTS/KILOMETRES PER HOUR'.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'CANCEL SPEED RESTRICTION' to remove a speed restriction.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'NO [ATC] SPEED RESTRICTIONS' to indicate no ATC speed restrictions apply.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'DO NOT EXCEED MACH (number)' to impose a maximum Mach number.
'Minimum clean speed' signifies the minimum speed at which an aircraft can be flown in a clean configuration, i.e. without deployment of lift-augmentation devices, speed brakes or landing gear.
Information regarding traffic on a conflicting path should be given, whenever practicable, in the following form.
Traffic information shall include the relative bearing of the conflicting traffic in terms of the 12-hour clock.
Traffic information shall include the distance from the conflicting traffic in kilometres or nautical miles.
Traffic information shall include the direction in which the conflicting traffic appears to be proceeding.
Traffic information shall include the level and type of aircraft, or if unknown, the relative speed of the conflicting traffic.

Traffic information templates follow the structure: [UNKNOWN/UNIDENTIFIED/ADDITIONAL] TRAFFIC (number) O’CLOCK (number) MILE[S]/KILOMETRES [DIRECTION] [CLIMBING/DESCENDING LEVEL] [LEVEL UNKNOWN] [(a/c type)] [SLOW/FAST MOVING] [YOUR CLEARED

Pilots may use the phrase 'REQUEST VECTORS' to request course guidance.
Pilots may use the phrase 'REQUEST AVOIDANCE ADVICE' to request avoiding action.
ATC may use the phrase 'DO YOU WANT VECTORS' to inquire if pilots desire course guidance.
ATC may use the phrase 'TURN LEFT/RIGHT [IMMEDIATELY] HEADING (three digits) TO AVOID [UNKNOWN/UNIDENTIFIED] TRAFFIC (bearing by clock-reference and distance)' to provide avoiding action.
ATC may use the phrase 'TURN LEFT/RIGHT (number) DEGREES IMMEDIATELY TO AVOID [UNKNOWN/UNIDENTIFIED] TRAFFIC AT (bearing by clock-reference and distance)' to provide avoiding action.
ATC may use the phrase 'SUGGEST [IMMEDIATE] LEFT/RIGHT TURN (numbers) DEGREES/HEADING (numbers)' to suggest avoiding action.
ATC may use the phrase 'CLEAR OF TRAFFIC [(appropriate instructions)]' to indicate traffic conflict is resolved.

Traffic information shall include the following elements of information as applicable: identification of the aircraft to which the information is transmitted, the words “TRAFFIC [IS]” or “ADDITIONAL TRAFFIC [IS]”, description of the traffic
Traffic information must include the identification of the aircraft to which the information is transmitted.
Traffic information must use the words “TRAFFIC [IS]” or “ADDITIONAL TRAFFIC [IS]”.
Traffic information must include a description of the traffic in terms that will facilitate recognition by the pilot, e.g. type, speed category, colour, type of vehicle, number of persons, etc.
Traffic information must include the position of the traffic relative to the aircraft concerned.
Traffic information must include the direction of movement.
Traffic information must include the level of traffic if applicable.
The order of elements in a traffic information message as provided above shall not be considered mandatory.
Circumstances may necessitate that single elements deemed to be important for avoiding a collision hazard are provided earlier than indicated in the listed order.

Wake turbulence category will only be essential traffic information (relating to controlled flights) if the aircraft concerned is of a heavier wake turbulence category than the aircraft to which the traffic information is directed.

Phraseology for position of traffic includes examples such as (A/C type) (position) FOR FULL STOP LANDING/ TOUCH AND GO/LOW APPROACH/SPOT LANDING, (A/C type) (position) OPPOSITE/CROSSING LEFT TO RIGHT/RIGHT TO LEFT/ SAME DIRECTION/OVERTAKIN

If no radio contact is established after a frequency change, ATC shall provide instructions using the phrase 'IF NO CONTACT (instructions)'.
ATC shall instruct an aircraft to change its call sign using the phrase 'CHANGE YOUR CALL SIGN TO (new call sign) [UNTIL FURTHER ADVISED]'.
ATC shall advise an aircraft to revert to its flight plan call sign using the phrase 'REVERT TO FLIGHT PLAN CALL SIGN (call sign) [AT (significant point)]'.

ATC shall issue holding instructions using phrases such as 'HOLD IN THE HOLDING PATTERN (designation) [AT (level)]', 'HOLD OVER (location) [AT (level)] [UNTIL (time)]', or 'JOIN HOLDING PATTERN (designation) [AT (level)]'.

ATC shall issue visual holding instructions using phrases such as 'HOLD VISUAL [OVER] (position)/BETWEEN (two prominent landmarks)', 'HOLD OVER (significant point, name of facility), AT (level), EXPECT APPROACH/FURTHER CLEARANCE AT (time)/I

ATC shall issue detailed holding instructions including clearance to a fix, level, holding direction/pattern, outbound time, and expected clearance time using the provided complex phraseology templates.

ATC may instruct the aircraft to report inbound/outbound status or commence approach at a specific time using phrases 'REPORT (name of facility or fix) INBOUND/OUTBOUND' or 'COMMENCE APPROACH AT (time)'.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'YOU ARE ENTERING AIRSPACE CHARLIE/DELTA' to warn a pilot of entry into controlled airspace.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'LEAVE AIRSPACE CHARLIE/DELTA DIRECTION/HEADING (digits) AT (level) (reason)' to instruct a pilot to leave controlled airspace.
A pilot shall use the phraseology 'LEAVING AIRSPACE CHARLIE/DELTA DIRECTION/HEADING (digits) AT (level)' to confirm departure from controlled airspace.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'YOU ARE LEAVING AIRSPACE CHARLIE/DELTA' to confirm a pilot's departure from controlled airspace.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'MIND DANGER AREA (description)' or 'AVOID RESTRICTED AREA (description)' to warn about other airspace hazards.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'STAY CLEAR OF (airspace, area)' or 'CONFIRM YOU WILL STAY CLEAR OF (airspace, area)' to instruct avoidance of specific airspace.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'YOU ARE APPROACHING AIRSPACE (class)' to warn a pilot of proximity to airspace.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'TRA (name) IS ACTIVE [FROM (level)] UP TO (level)' to inform pilots of active temporary reserved airspace.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'CLEARED TO CLIMB THROUGH AIRSPACE D/C' when clearing a pilot to climb through airspace until entering TRA.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'TRA (name) DEACTIVATED [AT (time)]' to inform pilots that a temporary reserved airspace is no longer active.
A pilot shall use the phraseology 'REQUEST QDM/QDR/QTE' to request direction finding information.
ATC shall provide direction finding information using the phraseology 'QDM/QDR/QTE (DF value)' when responding to a DF request.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'DF OUT OF SERVICE' to indicate that direction finding equipment is unavailable.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'TRANSMIT FOR DF' or 'TRANSMITTING FOR DF' to instruct a pilot to transmit for direction finding.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'EXPECT MILITARY [HONOUR] ESCORT [CAN YOU ACCEPT]' to inform a pilot of expected military escort.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'YOU WILL BE INTERCEPTED (information)' to inform a pilot of interception.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'SEPARATION MINIMA WILL NOT BE APPLIED' when interception is occurring and standard separation cannot be guaranteed.
More details regarding interception are provided in Appendix 1.
A pilot shall use 'REQUEST TO DROP BANNER' and ATC shall use 'CLEARED TO DROP [BANNER]' or 'BANNER DROPPING APPROVED' for banner dropping operations.
A pilot shall use 'REQUEST TO DROP PARACHUTE JUMPERS' and ATC shall use 'CLEARED TO DROP [DESCENT APPROVED]' or 'DROPPING APPROVED' for parachute drop operations.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'STAY ABOVE THE HIGHEST JUMPER [UNTIL [PASSING] (details)]' to instruct aircraft during parachute drops.
A pilot shall use the phraseology 'REQUEST AEROBATICS [OVERHEAD (location)/IN BOX] [(details)]' to request aerobatics clearance.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'AEROBATICS [OVERHEAD (location)/IN BOX] APPROVED [(details)]' to approve aerobatics.
ATC shall use the phraseology 'CLEARED AEROBATICS [OVERHEAD (location)/IN BOX] [(details)]' to clear a pilot for aerobatics.
When a pilot reports a state of minimum fuel, the controller shall inform the pilot as soon as practicable of any anticipated delays or that no delays are expected.
The phraseology for reporting minimum fuel is 'MINIMUM FUEL'. The controller's readback/response is 'ROGER' followed by delay information or 'NO DELAY EXPECTED'.

MINIMUM FUEL means a term used to describe a situation in which an aircraft's fuel supply has reached a state where the flight is committed to land at a specific aerodrome and no additional delay can be accepted.
The PAN PAN PAN call should not be used instead of the MINIMUM FUEL declaration.

When the level of fuel renders declaring a situation of distress necessary, the pilot shall indicate that by using the radiotelephony distress signal (MAYDAY), preferably spoken three times, followed by the nature of the distress condition
The phraseology for a fuel emergency declaration is 'MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY FUEL'.
To indicate a state of emergency, the pilot shall select Code 7700 unless ATC has previously directed the pilot to operate the transponder on a specified code.

If ATC has previously directed the pilot to operate the transponder on a specified code, the pilot may nevertheless select Code 7700 whenever there is a specific reason to believe that this would be the best course of action.
To indicate a state of radiocommunication failure, the pilot shall select Code 7600.
To indicate a state of unlawful interference, the pilot shall attempt to select Code 7500. If circumstances so warrant, Code 7700 should be used instead.
An aircraft shall be advised by the appropriate ATS unit to transfer from one radio frequency to another in accordance with agreed procedures.
In the absence of such advice, the aircraft shall notify the ATS unit before such a transfer takes place.

When establishing initial contact on, or when leaving a VHF frequency, an aircraft shall transmit such information as may be prescribed by the ANSP responsible for the provision of services and approved by the competent authority.
An aircraft station shall not leave a control frequency unless it has been requested to do so by the ATC unit or has received permission to do so.
An ATC unit may instruct an aircraft station to remain on the assigned frequency.
When communications are transferred from an air traffic service unit to another, this message shall contain the unit call sign and the frequency.
An air traffic service unit may advise an aircraft station to omit the prescribed parts of the initial call, except the aircraft call sign, by using the phrase “CALL SIGN ONLY”.
An aircraft may be requested to “STAND BY” on a frequency when it is intended that the ATS unit will initiate communications soon.
An aircraft may be requested to "MONITOR" a frequency when information is being broadcast thereon.
Air traffic control service is not provided at uncontrolled aerodromes.
The aerodrome frequency of uncontrolled aerodromes is mainly available to pilots for transmitting position reports.
Phraseologies regarding flight information shall only be used by appropriate ATS units.
Pilots shall use 'REQUEST TAXI INFORMATION [FROM HANGAR/APRON] [TO APRON/HANGAR]' to request taxi information.
Ground shall respond to taxi requests with 'TAXI AT OWN DISCRETION VIA (route)' or similar.

Pilots shall use 'READY FOR DEPARTURE REQUEST IFR CLEARANCE [SLOT(time)]' to request IFR clearance.

Ground shall use 'UNABLE TO ISSUE CLEARANCE (reasons)' if unable to issue clearance.
Ground shall use 'STAND BY FOR CLEARANCE' to request the pilot to wait.
Pilots shall use 'REQUEST DEPARTURE INFORMATION' to request departure information.
Ground shall provide runway, wind, and QNH information using 'RUNWAY (number) [SURFACE] WIND (direction, speed), QNH (number)' or 'WIND (number) DEGREES (number) KNOTS RUNWAY (number)' upon request.
Ground shall use 'REPORT WHEN READY [FOR DEPARTURE]' to ask the pilot to report readiness.
Pilots shall use 'READY [FOR DEPARTURE] RUNWAY (number)' to report readiness for departure.
Ground shall use 'TAKE OFF AT OWN DISCRETION [TRAFFIC IS (details)] [CAUTION (details)]' to authorize takeoff.
Pilots shall use 'REQUEST AIRBORNE TIME' to request airborne time, and Ground shall provide 'AIRBORNE (time)' in response.
Pilots shall use 'GOING AROUND' to announce a go-around.
Pilots shall use 'MAKING LOW APPROACH' to announce a low approach.
Pilots shall use 'MAKING SHORT/LONG LANDING' to announce short or long landing intentions.
Pilots shall use 'MAKING SPOT LANDINGS' to announce spot landing intentions.
Pilots shall use 'APPROACHING FOR BANNER PICK UP' to announce approach for banner pickup.
Pilots shall use 'APPROACHING FOR BANNER/ROPE DROP' to announce approach for banner/rope drop.
Pilots shall use 'FLYING [RIGHT [HAND]] [TRAFFIC] CIRCUIT[S]' to announce traffic circuit direction.
Pilots shall use 'MAKING TOUCH AND GO' to announce touch and go intentions.
Pilots shall use 'MAKING FULL STOP' to announce full stop intentions.
Pilots shall use 'LEAVING FREQUENCY' to announce leaving the frequency, and Ground shall respond with 'ROGER'.
Pilots shall use '(position report) [VFR FROM (location of departure)] REQUEST LANDING INFORMATION' to request landing information.
Ground shall use 'LAND AT OWN DISCRETION' to authorize landing, potentially preceded by traffic information.
Pilots shall use 'REQUEST LANDING TIME' to request landing time, and Ground shall provide 'LANDING TIME/ON GROUND (time)' in response.
An aircraft which is being subjected to unlawful interference shall endeavour to set the transponder to Code 7500.

An aircraft which is being subjected to unlawful interference shall notify the appropriate ATS unit of any significant circumstances associated therewith and any deviation from the current flight plan necessitated by the circumstances.
The station addressed by an aircraft being subjected to an act of unlawful interference, or first station acknowledging a call from such aircraft, shall render all possible assistance.

No special phraseologies are determined.
Communication related to direction finding comprises messages for the transmission of direction finding values in case a pilot has lost his orientation or to render other navigational assistance.
A direction finding station working alone can only determine the direction of an aircraft in relation to itself.
A direction finding station working alone should give QTE (true bearing of the aircraft) as requested, using the appropriate phrase.

A direction finding station working alone should give QUJ (true heading to be steered by the aircraft, with no wind, to head for the direction finding station) as requested, using the appropriate phrase.
A direction finding station working alone should give QDR (magnetic bearing of the aircraft) as requested, using the appropriate phrase.
A direction finding station working alone should give QDM (magnetic heading to be steered by the aircraft with no wind to make for the station) as requested, using the appropriate phrase.
When a heading or bearing has been requested, the direction finding station shall advise the aircraft station with the appropriate phrase.

When a heading or bearing has been requested, the direction finding station shall advise the aircraft station with the bearing or heading in degrees in relation to the direction-finding station, sent as three figures.
When a heading or bearing has been requested, the direction finding station shall advise the aircraft station with the class of bearing.
When a heading or bearing has been requested, the direction finding station may advise the aircraft station with the time of observation if necessary.
Class A bearing accuracy is accurate within plus or minus 2 degrees.
Class B bearing accuracy is accurate within plus or minus 5 degrees.
An urgency message shall be transmitted on the air-ground frequency in use at the time.
An urgency message shall consist of as many of the following elements as required: name of ATS unit, aircraft ID, nature of urgency, pilot intention, position/level/heading, and other useful info.
The radiotelephony urgency signal 'PAN PAN' shall be preferably spoken three times, with each word pronounced as the French word 'panne'.
The ATS unit addressed in an urgency message will normally be that ATS unit communicating with the aircraft or in whose area of responsibility the aircraft is operating.
Provisions for urgency messages are not intended to prevent an aircraft from broadcasting an urgency message if time and circumstances render this course preferable.

Useful information in an urgency message may include remaining aircraft endurance/fuel, number of persons on board, possible presence of hazardous materials, aircraft colour/markings, and survival aids.
The ATS unit addressed by an aircraft reporting an urgency condition or the first ATS unit acknowledging the urgency message shall acknowledge the urgency message.

The ATS unit addressed by an aircraft reporting an urgency condition or the first ATS unit acknowledging the urgency message shall, if necessary, exercise control of communications.

The requirement to inform the aircraft operating agency concerned does not have priority over any other action which involves the safety of the flight in distress, or of any other flight in the area, or which might affect the progress of ex
Urgency communications have priority over all other communications except distress communications.
All ATS units and aircraft shall take care not to interfere with the transmission of urgency traffic.

The use of the signal described in point 4.1.3.4.2 shall indicate that the message which follows concerns a protected medical transport pursuant to the 1949 Geneva Conventions and Additional Protocols.

For announcing and identifying aircraft used for medical transports, a transmission of the radiotelephony urgency signal 'PAN PAN' shall be followed by the radiotelephony signal for medical transports 'MAY-DEE-CAL'.
The message concerning a protected medical transport shall convey the call sign or other recognised means of identification of the medical transports.
The message concerning a protected medical transport shall convey the position of the medical transports.
The message concerning a protected medical transport shall convey the number and type of the medical transports.
The message concerning a protected medical transport shall convey the intended route.
The message concerning a protected medical transport shall convey the estimated time en-route and of departure and arrival, as appropriate.

The message concerning a protected medical transport shall convey any other information such as flight altitude, radio frequencies guarded, languages used and secondary surveillance radar modes and codes.
The provisions of points 4.1.3.2. and 4.1.3.3. shall apply as appropriate to ATS units receiving a medical transports message.
The VHF emergency frequency (121,500 MHz) shall be used for genuine emergency purposes.
The VHF emergency frequency shall be used to provide a clear channel between aircraft in distress or emergency and a ground station when the normal channels are being utilised for other aircraft.

The VHF emergency frequency shall be used to provide a VHF communication channel between aircraft and aerodromes, not normally used by international air services, in case of an emergency condition arising.

Aircraft in the traffic circuit shall be controlled to provide the separation minima outlined in 7.9.2, 7.10.1 and 7.11 and Chapter 5, Section 5.8.
Aircraft in formation are exempted from the separation minima with respect to separation from other aircraft of the same flight.
Aircraft operating in different areas or different runways on aerodromes suitable for simultaneous landings or take-offs are exempted from the separation minima.
Separation minima shall not apply to aircraft operating under military necessity in accordance with Chapter 16, Section 16.1.

Sufficient separation shall be effected between aircraft in flight in the traffic circuit to allow the spacing of arriving and departing aircraft as outlined in 7.9.2, 7.10.1 and 7.11 and Chapter 5, Section 5.8.

Separation minima may be reduced in the vicinity of aerodromes for one aircraft following another if the flight crew of the succeeding aircraft reports that the other aircraft is in sight and separation can be maintained.

If a pilot is not familiar with an instrument approach procedure, the ATC unit shall specify the initial approach level, turn points, procedure turn level, and final approach track.
If the aircraft is cleared for a straight-in approach, only the final approach track need be specified regarding turn parameters.
The frequency(ies) of navigation aids and the missed approach procedure shall be specified when deemed necessary.
The entire instrument approach procedure must be executed even if visual reference is established, unless the aircraft requests and is cleared for a visual approach.
In the event of extended delays, aircraft should be advised of the anticipated delay as early as possible.
When practicable, aircraft should be instructed or given the option to reduce speed en route to absorb delay.
When delay is expected, the ACC shall normally be responsible for clearing aircraft to the holding fix and including holding instructions and expected approach time or onward clearance time.
After coordination with the approach control unit, the ACC may clear an arriving aircraft to a visual holding location.
After coordination with the aerodrome control tower, the approach control unit may clear an arriving aircraft to a visual holding location.

Aircraft should normally be held at a designated holding fix.

Criteria and procedures for the simultaneous use of adjacent holding patterns shall be prescribed in local instructions.
Levels at a holding fix or visual holding location shall as far as practicable be assigned in a manner that will facilitate clearing each aircraft to approach in its proper priority.
Normally, the first aircraft to arrive over a holding fix or visual holding location should be at the lowest level, with following aircraft at successively higher levels.

When extended holding is anticipated, turbojet aircraft should, when practicable, be permitted to hold at higher levels in order to conserve fuel, while retaining their order in the approach sequence.
If an aircraft is unable to comply with the published or cleared holding procedure, alternative instructions shall be issued.
An aircraft may be instructed to orbit at its present or any other position to maintain safe and orderly traffic flow, provided required obstacle clearance is ensured.

A trend-type landing forecast shall be included in the meteorological information, when available.

Changes in the operational status of visual and non-visual aids essential for approach and landing shall be transmitted.

During final approach, the specified information shall be transmitted without delay.
The sudden occurrence of hazards (e.g. unauthorized traffic on the runway) shall be transmitted without delay during final approach.
Significant variations in the current surface wind, expressed in terms of minimum and maximum values, shall be transmitted without delay during final approach.
Significant changes in runway surface conditions shall be transmitted without delay during final approach.
Changes in the operational status of required visual or non-visual aids shall be transmitted without delay during final approach.

Priority shall be given to an aircraft which anticipates being compelled to land because of factors affecting the safe operation of the aircraft.

Priority shall be given to aircraft engaged in search and rescue operations.
Priority shall be given to other aircraft as may be determined by the appropriate authority.

Upon recognition that an aircraft is making an emergency descent, all appropriate action shall be taken immediately to safeguard all aircraft concerned.

The pilot shall take the following steps as soon as practicable in the order appropriate for the circumstance during an emergency descent.

The pilot shall turn on aircraft exterior lights (commensurate with appropriate operating limitations).
The pilot shall watch for conflicting traffic both visually and by reference to ACAS (if equipped).
When emergency descent is complete, the pilot shall coordinate further intentions with the appropriate ATS unit.
